slides.title: Most workers feel burned out, and 43% are at risk of quitting

exhibits.heading: I feel burned out from work

slides.soWhat: Half the workforce is one offer away from leaving; retention is a manager problem before it is a pay problem.
slides.source: Future of work survey, October 2026; 4,985 deskless workers in four countries

callout.text: Agreement is the top two boxes; the strongly-agree share is the group that leaves first, and it is the one retention work has to reach.

slides.subtitle: Agreement with each statement, % of workers surveyed, 2025
note: Agreement is the top two boxes of a five-point scale
Base: 2,140 workers across eleven markets, September 2025

slides.title: Investors want companies to keep investing while delivering on guidance

items.title: Investors that believe it is important to prioritize building business capabilities, even at the expense of delivering EPS
items.text: Near the series average of 89%, and below the June survey result of 91%

items.title: Investors that feel it is important to deliver on EPS guidance and consensus forecasts
items.text: Near the series high of 87%, and above the February result of 71%

callout.text: While investors have consistently supported investing in the business at the expense of EPS, they now also expect companies to fully deliver on guidance and consensus.

slides.subtitle: Investor preference between investing in the business and delivering EPS, 2025
points: Investors back investment over EPS by a wide margin
They now expect guidance to be met as well
The two expectations are held at once, which is new
